sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221], with operating income growing faster at a 20.5% CAGR [F223].
The window is a compounding cloud story rather than a cycle: growth held between 13.6% and 18.0% in every year except FY2023, when it slowed to 6.9% [D152][D258][D311][D472].

FY2026 was the sharpest step, revenue up 17.8% [D472], driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud led by Azure and Productivity and Business Processes by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [P17].
The FY2023 slowdown came as revenue rose only 6.9% [D311], driven by Intelligent Cloud and Productivity and Business Processes offset by a decline in More Personal Computing [P39].
Microsoft Cloud supplied 16.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth [D568][D472] and reached 64.6% of revenue [D566].
Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp in FY2026 [D642], as revenue rose 31% driven by Azure and other cloud services [P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services contributed 5.1pp in FY2026 [D649], while XBOX subtracted 0.6pp as its revenue fell 7.1% [D713][D712].
Operating leverage was strong: incremental operating margin was 53.3% in FY2026 [D498], and operating costs grew 10.3pp slower than revenue [D499], at 7.4% [D491].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against net income growth of 31.3% in FY2026 [D476][D474], with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D493].
Operating margin reached 46.8% in FY2026, a window high and 5.1pp above the 41.7% window median [F50][D974][D975], while gross margin of 67.9% sat below its 68.2% median [F30][D981].
The FY2026 operating margin rose 1.2pp [D487], with cost of revenue costing 0.9pp, R&D adding 0.8pp and other lines adding 1.2pp [D500][D501][D502].
The cost-of-revenue drag reflects continued investments in AI infrastructure and a sales mix shift to Azure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure [P11].
In FY2026 net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below the 46.8% operating margin [F70][F50][D1023], as other income of $10.7 billion included $6.5 billion of net gains on OpenAI investments [X124][P7].
Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income in FY2026, above the 1.34x window median [F100][F60][D459][D1013].

Free cash flow of $67.0 billion was only 0.50x net income, the window low against a 0.91x median [F120][F60][D460][D990], as capex of $115.9 billion reached 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x D&A [F110][D455][D461].
Cash used in investing rose $66.9 billion to $139.5 billion, primarily on a $51.4 billion increase in additions to property and equipment [P1].
Free cash flow margin fell to 20.2%, the window low against a 30.3% median [D456][D984], and sits at the 20th percentile against a 34.7% software peer median [D1002][D1003].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, or 22.0% of revenue [D465][D466], against a -7.2% software peer median and in the 83rd percentile of six peers [D1007][D1006].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion [D464][D495], while the current ratio of 1.23x is the window low against a 1.93x median [F200][D991][D993].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion consumed 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468], and the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D493].
The net cash cushion and shrinking debt leave room for the capex programme, but the 1.23x current ratio is the thinnest liquidity position in the window [F200][D991].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at 0.70x and 0.50x [D406][D460], as capex rose 79.6% in FY2026 [D479].
This is the flag that matters: the gap is capex-driven and widening, so free cash flow now converts half of earnings [D460].
The pack's liquidity series omits short-term investments in FY2017, so net cash and cash-and-investments growth across that gap are not comparable [R6].
That break affects only the FY2017-to-FY2018 comparison, not the later trend [R6].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the 20.2% FY2026 low [D456], reported in the FY2027 10-K cash flow section.
Whether capex as a share of revenue falls back below the 34.9% FY2026 level [D455], disclosed in the FY2027 10-K investing section.
Whether operating margin holds above the 46.8% FY2026 high [D974], shown in the FY2027 10-K results of operations.
